definition.cn: “给某人找麻烦” 或 “让某人不好过”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from everyday scenarios where one person makes another's life difficult or unpleasant. It is commonly used to describe a deliberate action that causes stress, inconvenience, or annoyance to another person.

examples.en: He likes to give his little brother a hard time by teasing him constantly.
examples.cn: 他喜欢通过不断地戏弄他的弟弟来给他找麻烦。

examples.en: My boss always gives me a hard time for being a few minutes late.
examples.cn: 我老板总是因为我迟到几分钟而给我找麻烦。

examples.en: Don't give her a hard time; she's trying her best.
examples.cn: 别让她不好过；她已经尽力了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于日常生活中，当一个人使另一个人的生活变得困难或令人不愉快时，就会用到这个表达。它常用于描述一种人为的、故意的对其他人造成压力、不便或烦扰的行为。

title: Give someone a piece of my mind

definition.cn: “严厉斥责某人” 或 “直言不讳地批评某人”。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to the 16th century, when "giving someone a piece of one's mind" meant giving them a very direct personal opinion, often negative or angry. In modern English, this phrase is typically used to describe expressing strong discontent or disapproval toward someone's behavior or attitude.

examples.en: After being late again, his boss gave him a piece of her mind.
examples.cn: 在他再次迟到后，他的老板严厉斥责了他。

examples.en: She gave the rude customer a piece of her mind.
examples.cn: 她严厉斥责了那个无礼的顾客。

examples.en: He decided to give his roommate a piece of his mind about the mess.
examples.cn: 他决定严厉批评他的室友关于房间的混乱。

origin.cn: 这个短语可以追溯到16世纪，当时 “给某人一块自己的心情” 意味着给他们一种非常直接的个人意见，通常是负面的或愤怒的。在现代英语中，这个短语通常用来描述表达某人对某人行为或态度的强烈不满。

title: Give someone a song and dance

definition.en: This idiom originally comes from classic American theater, where performers would use exaggerated singing and dancing to distract or cover something up. Over time, it began to describe the act of creating elaborate and untruthful excuses or explanations to deceive or mislead someone.

examples.en: When asked why he was late, he gave them a song and dance about traffic.
examples.cn: 当被问及为什么迟到时，他编了一堆关于交通的瞎话。

examples.en: I don't want your song and dance; just tell me the truth.
examples.cn: 我不想听你的借口；直接告诉我真相吧。

examples.en: She gave the teacher a song and dance about why she didn't do her homework.
examples.cn: 她向老师编了一堆不做作业的借口。

origin.cn: 这个习语中的 “song and dance” 最早源自美国剧院中的古典讽刺表演，艺术家们通过歌唱和跳舞来夸大或掩饰某些事情。后来，这个短语开始用来形容为某件事情编造不真实且复杂的借口或解释，企图迷惑或误导他人。

definition.en: This phrase comes from medieval law practices when criminals were quickly judged and executed, with only a brief time given for confession (shrift). In modern use, it means to not take someone or something seriously, giving it little attention or time.

examples.en: The manager gave her complaint short shrift and moved on to the next task.
examples.cn: 经理对她的投诉草草了事，然后继续处理下一个任务。

examples.en: When the idea was proposed, it was given short shrift by the board.
examples.cn: 当这个想法被提出时，董事会敷衍了事。

examples.en: Her concerns were given short shrift in the meeting.
examples.cn: 她的担忧在会议上被草草了事。

origin.cn: 这一短语源于中世纪的法律实践，当罪犯被迅速判决并处决时，他们仅允许简短的忏悔时间（shrift）。现代的用法是指不认真对待某人或某事，不给予足够的关注或时间。

title: Give someone the benefit of the doubt

definition.cn: “把好处归于未知的一方” 或 “姑且相信某人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the legal principle of presumption of innocence, where if there isn't enough evidence to prove someone's guilt, the judicial system will choose to believe the person is innocent. This expression has been widely used to indicate that, in the absence of definitive evidence, one chooses to believe someone's good intentions or honesty.

examples.en: I didn't see who took the money, so I'll give him the benefit of the doubt.
examples.cn: 我没有看到是谁拿了钱，所以我姑且相信是他。

examples.en: She might be late, but I'll give her the benefit of the doubt this time.
examples.cn: 她可能会迟到，但这次我会姑且相信她。

examples.en: Even though the explanation seems odd, I'll give you the benefit of the doubt.
examples.cn: 尽管这个解释听起来很奇怪，但我姑且相信你。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于司法系统中的无罪推定原则。在没有足够证据证明某人有罪的情况下，司法系统通常会选择相信被告是无辜的。这个短语已经被广泛使用，表示在没有明确证据的情况下，选择相信某人的好意或诚信。

definition.cn: “冷落某人” 或 “对某人爱理不理”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the Middle Ages when a guest who was not well-received might be given cold food or a cold shoulder of mutton, indicating that they were no longer welcome. This action symbolized rejection and distancing. "Give someone the cold shoulder" has become widely used to describe treating someone with indifference or intentionally ignoring them.

examples.en: After their argument, she gave him the cold shoulder all week.
examples.cn: 争吵过后，她整整一周都对他冷眼相对。

examples.en: I can't believe he would give me the cold shoulder after all we've been through.
examples.cn: 我无法相信在我们经历了这么多之后，他会冷落我。

examples.en: If you're unhappy, don't just give me the cold shoulder—let's talk about it.
examples.cn: 如果你不开心，不要只是冷落我——我们谈谈吧。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于中世纪，当时如果一位客人在主人的家中受到了冷落，他可能会被提供冷的食物或冷的肩肉（通常是羊肩肉），表示不再受欢迎。这个动作象征了拒绝与疏远。"Give someone the cold shoulder" 已经广泛用于形容冷淡对待或故意忽视某人。

definition.en: This phrase originated in the 19th century, meaning to escape from a place or situation that others do not want you to leave, often using clever means. During that time, if someone "slipped you a note", it implied secretly providing information, hence "give them the slip" evolved to mean escaping or shaking off.

examples.en: We had to give them the slip to avoid being caught.
examples.cn: 我们不得不甩开他们以免被抓住。

examples.en: She managed to give the paparazzi the slip.
examples.cn: 她成功地甩开了狗仔队。

examples.en: The thief gave the police the slip and disappeared into the crowd.
examples.cn: 小偷甩开了警察并消失在人群中。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪，意指通过巧妙的手段从某个别人不想你离开的场合逃脱。在那时，如果有人用 “给你一张纸条（slip you a note）” 等同于偷偷摸摸给信息，因此 “给他们纸条” 逐渐演变为 “摆脱他们”。

definition.en: This phrase originates from woodworking terminology. In woodworking, cutting along the grain is the easiest and most effective, while cutting against the grain is laborious and may cause the wood to splinter. Therefore, this expression gradually came to describe doing things in a way that defies convention or is uniquely different.

examples.en: He always likes to go against the grain and do things differently.
examples.cn: 他总喜欢逆势而为，用不同的方式做事。

examples.en: Her decision to travel alone goes against the grain of what her family expects.
examples.cn: 她独自旅行的决定与家人的期望背道而驰。

examples.en: It's challenging to go against the grain, but sometimes it's necessary for innovation.
examples.cn: 虽然逆势而为充满挑战，但有时候为了创新这是必要的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于木工加工中的术语。在木工中，沿着木纹切割是最容易和最有效的，而逆着木纹切割（go against the grain）则费力且可能导致木材破裂。因此，这个表达逐渐用来形容做事不顺从常理，或与众不同的方式。

definition.en: This idiom originates from the idea of moving in a circular path without making any real progress, representing repetitive actions without achieving productive results. It is often used to describe situations where people continue doing the same thing without making effective progress in solving a problem or completing a task.

examples.en: We've been trying to solve this issue for hours, but we’re just going around in circles.
examples.cn: 我们已经试图解决这个问题好几个小时了，但结果只是原地打转。

examples.en: If we keep arguing without finding a solution, we’re just going around in circles.
examples.cn: 如果我们继续争论而不找到解决方案，那只是徒劳无功。

examples.en: I feel like this meeting is just going around in circles with no clear direction.
examples.cn: 我觉得这个会议只是原地打转，没有明确的方向。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于一种毫无方向感的状态，形象地表示反复进行某种活动却无法得出实际成果。通常用来形容人们在处理问题或任务时，没有找到有效的解决方案，来回反复地做同样的事而没有进展。

title: Go back to the drawing board

definition.en: This phrase originates from the fields of design and engineering, typically used when a draft or plan is unsatisfactory or unsuccessful. Going back to the drawing board means you need to replan and redesign to find a better solution. In modern society, this idiom is widely applied across various fields to indicate that a failed plan requires a fresh start.

examples.en: The project didn’t work out as expected, so we have to go back to the drawing board.
examples.cn: 项目没有按预期进行，所以我们必须重新开始。

examples.en: If this strategy fails, we’ll need to go back to the drawing board.
examples.cn: 如果这个策略失败了，我们就需要重新开始。

examples.en: After reviewing the feedback, they decided to go back to the drawing board and revise their approach.
examples.cn: 在审查反馈意见后，他们决定重新开始并修改他们的方法。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于设计和工程领域，通常在图纸绘制不满意或计划未能成功时使用。回到绘图板意味着需要重新规划和设计，以便找到更好的解决方案。在现代社会，这个习语被广泛应用于各种领域，表示某个计划失败，需要从头再来。

definition.en: This phrase originated in American slang in the mid-20th century and is often used to describe someone who suddenly becomes extremely excited, angry, or exhibits irrational behavior. There are various explanations for its exact origin, but one common theory is that it is related to the way monkeys act excitedly around bananas.

examples.en: The kids went bananas when they heard about the trip to Disneyland.
examples.cn: 孩子们听到要去迪士尼乐园的消息后变得非常兴奋。

examples.en: Her mother went bananas when she saw the mess in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 她妈妈看到厨房的凌乱后非常生气。

examples.en: Fans go bananas whenever their favorite team wins a match.
examples.cn: 每当他们喜欢的球队赢得比赛时，粉丝们都会变得狂热。

origin.cn: “Go bananas” 这个短语来源于20世纪中期的美国俚语，常被用来形容某人突然变得非常兴奋、愤怒或是表现出非理性的行为。关于该短语的确切起源有很多说法，但其中一种较为普遍的解释是它与猴子喜欢香蕉有关，因为看到香蕉时猴子显得特别激动和疯狂。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the imagery of fish turning belly up when they die, floating on the water surface with their bellies facing up, signifying they are dead. Thus, the expression is used to describe a business or project that has completely failed. In modern English, this is often used to refer to business bankruptcy or the complete failure of an endeavor.

examples.en: The company went belly up after years of financial trouble.
examples.cn: 这家公司在多年财务困境后终于倒闭了。

examples.en: Many restaurants went belly up during the economic downturn.
examples.cn: 许多餐馆在经济衰退期间倒闭了。

examples.en: Our startup could go belly up if we don't get more investors soon.
examples.cn: 如果我们不尽快找到更多投资者，我们的初创公司可能会倒闭。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自鱼类死亡后会四肢朝天漂浮在水面上的情景，显得它们的肚子 (belly) 朝上 (up)，因此用于形容企业或项目彻底失败和崩溃。在现代英语中，这个表达通常用于指企业破产或事情彻底失败。

definition.en: This phrase originates from slang appearing around the 1940s, meaning to lose control or act unusually. Although "bonkers" is a somewhat humorous term, it is typically used to describe someone who becomes excessively agitated or out of control due to stress, anxiety, or other reasons. This expression is often used to depict people's emotional outbursts in certain situations, whether from excessive happiness, anger, or anxiety.

examples.en: She went bonkers when she won the lottery.
examples.cn: 当她中彩票时，她变得非常疯狂。

examples.en: The kids are going to go bonkers if they find out about the surprise party.
examples.cn: 如果孩子们发现有惊喜派对，他们会疯狂的。

examples.en: After working all week without a break, he finally went bonkers.
examples.cn: 连续一周不休息的工作让他终于发疯了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于俚语，它最早出现在20世纪40年代，意为失去控制或行为异常。虽然 “bonkers” 是一个具有滑稽意味的词，但它通常用来描述人们因压力、焦虑或其他原因而变得异常激动或失控。这种表达常用于形容人在某些情境下的情绪失控，既可以是开心过度，也可以是因为愤怒或焦虑。

definition.cn: “突然完全戒掉” 或 “立即戒断”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the process of quitting drugs or alcohol, indicating the sudden complete stop of using a substance instead of a gradual reduction. The body immediately exhibits withdrawal symptoms, similar to feeling as cold as turkey meat, hence the term "go cold turkey". Nowadays, it is widely used to describe abruptly stopping any habit or behavior.

examples.en: He decided to go cold turkey on smoking after 20 years.
examples.cn: 抽了 20 年烟后，他决定彻底戒掉烟瘾。

examples.en: After realizing how much time she spent online, she went cold turkey on social media.
examples.cn: 意识到自己在网上花了太多时间后，她决定彻底戒掉社交媒体。

examples.en: It's hard to go cold turkey on caffeine, but he managed to do it.
examples.cn: 完全戒掉咖啡因很难，但他做到了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自戒毒或戒酒的过程，指不通过渐进的方法，而是突然完全停止使用某种物质。因为身体会立即出现戒断反应，类似于感到冰冷的鸡肉，所以称之为 “go cold turkey”。如今，这个表达被广泛用于描述任何突然停止某种习惯或行为的情景。

definition.en: This phrase originates from aviation terminology, where a plane that gets hit or suffers mechanical failure may burn and crash to the ground. In modern usage, this phrase metaphorically describes a plan, project, or task that ends in a spectacularly unsuccessful manner.

examples.en: The business idea went down in flames after investors pulled out.
examples.cn: 投资者退出后，这个商业计划彻底失败了。

examples.en: Their attempt to negotiate a lower price went down in flames.
examples.cn: 他们试图谈判降低价格的努力彻底崩溃了。

examples.en: The project went down in flames due to poor planning and execution.
examples.cn: 由于糟糕的计划和执行，这个项目彻底失败了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到航空术语，当飞机被击中或机械故障导致坠毁时，通常会燃烧并坠于地面。在现代使用中，这个短语用来比喻一个计划、项目或任务以极不成功的方式结束。

definition.en: This phrase originated in the early 20th century in the United States. When someone is annoyed or upset with another person, they might tell them to go do something seemingly pointless, such as flying a kite. By saying this, they are essentially telling the person to leave them alone and stop bothering them.

examples.en: When he wouldn't stop arguing, I told him to go fly a kite.
examples.cn: 当他不停争论时，我叫他去放风筝。

examples.en: She was so annoying that I finally said, "Just go fly a kite!"
examples.cn: 她太烦人了，我最终说 “去放风筝吧！”

examples.en: He told me to go fly a kite when I asked for help.
examples.cn: 当我请求帮助时，他叫我去放风筝。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自20世纪初的美国。当某人对另一人感到厌烦或生气时，可能会礼貌地或不太礼貌地告诉他们去做一些看似无意义的事情，比如去放风筝。通过这样的表达，他们希望对方离开自己，不再打扰自己。

definition.cn: “去炸个蛋吧”，意指 “别烦我” 或 “去忙你自己的事”。
definition.en: This phrase is a lively expression in English similar to telling someone to "get lost" or "mind their own business." It emerged in the early 20th century, likely as a humorous or sarcastic method to get someone to stop bothering you. For example, when someone keeps pestering you, you might use it to tell them to back off.

examples.en: He kept asking me questions, so finally, I told him to go fry an egg.
examples.cn: 他一直问我问题，所以最后我让他去炸个蛋。

examples.en: If you're not going to help, just go fry an egg!
examples.cn: 如果你不打算帮忙，就去炸个蛋吧！

examples.en: When he started complaining again, she told him to go fry an egg and stop whining.
examples.cn: 当他再次开始抱怨时，她让他去炸个蛋，别再发牢骚了。

origin.cn: 这个短语在英语中是一个较为生动的表达，类似于中文中的 “走开点” 或 “去一边待着”。它最早出现在20世纪初，可能是作为一种幽默或讽刺的方式来劝阻某人停止烦扰。例如，当别人一直打扰你时，你可能会用它来表达让对方不要继续干扰自己。

definition.en: This idiom originates from the 19th century when farmers used a wire called "haywire" to bundle hay. These wires often became tangled and difficult to manage due to frequent use. Hence, the phrase came to be used to denote something becoming chaotic or out of control, no longer functioning as it should.

examples.en: Everything went haywire when the system crashed.
examples.cn: 系统崩溃后，一切都乱套了。

examples.en: My plans for the weekend went haywire due to the bad weather.
examples.cn: 由于天气恶劣，我的周末计划全都失控了。

examples.en: The robot started to go haywire and wouldn't stop moving.
examples.cn: 机器人开始失控，并且不停地移动。

origin.cn: “Go haywire” 这个短语源自于19世纪，当时的农民们使用一种叫做 “干草电线”（haywire）的铁丝将干草捆绑在一起。这些铁丝常常会因为使用频繁而缠绕在一起，成为杂乱无章、难以处理的状态。因此，这个短语后来用以表示某事物变得混乱失控、不再按照正常情况运行。

definition.cn: “单独行动” 或 “独自做某事”。
definition.en: This phrase means to take action alone or to accomplish something independently, without seeking help from others. It is often used to emphasize a person's independence and self-reliance. The expression first appeared in the early 20th century and is commonly used in contexts where someone decides to take full responsibility for a business, work, or personal project without relying on a team.

examples.en: He decided to go it alone and start his own business.
examples.cn: 他决定单干，开自己的公司。

examples.en: Sometimes you have to go it alone to achieve your goals.
examples.cn: 有时候，你必须独自行动才能实现自己的目标。

examples.en: She prefers to go it alone rather than work in a group.
examples.cn: 她宁愿单独行动，而不是在团队中工作。

origin.cn: 这个短语的意思是一个人独自采取行动或独自完成某事，而不寻求他人的帮助。这种表达通常用来强调个人的独立性和自主能力。它最早出现在20世纪初，通常用在描述一个人在商业、工作或个人项目中决定不借助团队，独自承担所有责任和任务的场景中。

definition.cn: “未做好准备就行动” 或 “鲁莽行事”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the mechanism of old firearms. If the gun's trigger was not fully cocked (i.e., in a "half-cocked" state), it could misfire or discharge unexpectedly, leading to unintended consequences. Thus, "Go off half-cocked" has come to mean acting hastily or rashly without proper preparation or thought.

examples.en: He always goes off half-cocked before knowing all the facts.
examples.cn: 他总是在没有了解所有事实之前就鲁莽行动。

examples.en: Don't go off half-cocked; make sure you have all the information first.
examples.cn: 不要贸然行事；确保你先掌握所有信息。

examples.en: She went off half-cocked with her complaint, not realizing the full context.
examples.cn: 她对情况不了解就贸然投诉了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于旧式火枪的发射机制。如果火枪的扳机没有完全扣紧（即 “半扣” 状态），可能会导致意外走火，没有达到预期效果。因而，“Go off half-cocked” 引申为在没有充分准备或考虑的情况下仓促行事、冒失行动。

definition.cn: “失去冷静” 或 “失去理智”。这个短语指一个人在情绪上突然崩溃或变得非常生气，通常表现出非理性的行为。
definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to swimming pools, which usually have a shallow end and a deep end. The shallow end is safer, while the deep end requires higher swimming skills. If someone jumps into the deep end unprepared, they might feel panicked and out of control, which is used here as a metaphor for emotional breakdown.

examples.en: When he heard the bad news, he just went off the deep end and started shouting.
examples.cn: 当他听到坏消息时，他简直失去了理智，开始大喊大叫。

examples.en: Don’t go off the deep end. Let's figure this out calmly.
examples.cn: 别失去冷静，我们冷静地解决这个问题。

examples.en: She went off the deep end when she found out her project had been canceled.
examples.cn: 当她得知项目被取消时，她失去了冷静。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到游泳池的深水区。游泳池通常有浅水区和深水区，浅水区较安全，而深水区则需要更高的游泳技能。一个人如果没有准备就跳入深水区，可能会感到慌乱和失控，借此比喻人情绪上的失控。

title: Go on a wild goose chase

definition.cn: “徒劳无功的追寻” 或 “白费功夫的寻找”。
definition.en: This phrase originally comes from 16th-century English literature, signifying that chasing wild geese is futile because of their unpredictable flight patterns. As a result, it describes actions that waste time and effort without any fruitful outcome.

examples.en: We went on a wild goose chase trying to find that old book.
examples.cn: 我们白费功夫地寻找那本旧书。

examples.en: She sent me on a wild goose chase looking for that nonexistent restaurant.
examples.cn: 她让我费尽心力去找那不存在的餐馆。

examples.en: Following that clue turned out to be a wild goose chase.
examples.cn: 追寻那个线索结果是徒劳无功的。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早起源于16世纪的英国文学，意指追赶野生鹅是徒劳无功的，因为它们飞行的方向变化无常且不可预测。因此，这个短语被用来形容那些耗费时间和精力却没有任何结果的行动。

examples.en: She really went out of her way to make sure everyone felt comfortable at the party.
examples.cn: 她真的竭尽全力确保每个人在聚会上都感到舒服。

examples.en: My boss went out of his way to help me with the project.
examples.cn: 我的老板不遗余力地帮助我完成了这个项目。

examples.en: They went out of their way to make our visit enjoyable.
examples.cn: 他们竭尽全力让我们的拜访变得愉快。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古英语中 “way” 代表道路或途径，而 “go out of one’s way” 则表示脱离正常路径去完成某事。它意味着为了达成目标或者帮助别人，做出超出常规的努力和牺牲。 **This phrase originates from Old English where "way" means road or path, and "go out of one’s way" refers to stepping off the normal path to accomplish something. It signifies making extra effort and sacrifice in order to achieve a goal or help someone.**

definition.cn: “冒险做某事” 或 “承担风险”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the idea of climbing a tree and standing on a limb (a branch), where the further out you go the less stable and more risky it becomes. In modern usage, "go out on a limb" means to take a risk or put oneself in a vulnerable position for a particular purpose, often to offer support or give an opinion.

examples.en: I'm going to go out on a limb and say that our team will win the championship this year.
examples.cn: 我要冒险说一句，我们的球队今年会赢得冠军。

examples.en: She went out on a limb to defend her friend in the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会议上冒险为她的朋友辩护。

examples.en: He decided to go out on a limb and invest in the startup company.
examples.cn: 他决定冒险投资那家初创公司。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于爬树时站在一根树枝上，即使站在树枝的末端会更加不稳定和危险。在现代社会，该短语用来形容一个人愿意冒风险或承担责任去做某事，通常是在给予某种支持或意见时。

definition.en: This phrase originates from nautical terminology, meaning someone falls over the side of a boat into the water. Figuratively, it means to do something excessively or to get carried away beyond reasonable limits in both actions and emotions.

examples.en: Don't go overboard with the decorations; we want a simple look.
examples.cn: 不要把装饰弄得太夸张了；我们想要简洁的样子。

examples.en: He tends to go overboard when buying gifts for his kids.
examples.cn: 他在给孩子买礼物时往往会做得过火。

examples.en: I appreciate your enthusiasm, but try not to go overboard with the planning.
examples.cn: 我很感激你的热情，但计划时别太过火了。

origin.cn: 这个短语来自航海术语，指的是人从船上掉进水中。比喻的意思是指某人做事情太过分或表现得过于极端，在行为和情绪上超越了合理的限度。

definition.en: This phrase originated in the 1980s in the United States following several instances where postal workers committed acts of workplace violence due to excessive stress. Although such incidents were not widespread, "go postal" has since become an expression used to describe someone suddenly going into a violent rage or losing control.

examples.en: When traffic is this bad, I feel like I'm about to go postal.
examples.cn: 当交通如此糟糕时，我感觉我快要发疯了。

examples.en: He went postal when he found out they had crashed his car.
examples.cn: 当他发现他们撞了他的车时，他暴怒了。

examples.en: The boss will go postal if the report isn't finished by tomorrow.
examples.cn: 如果报告明天之前还没完成，老板会发疯的。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪80年代美国邮政服务的员工由于过度压力而发生的几起暴力事件。当时几名邮局员工在工作场所大开杀戒，引发了极大的社会关注。尽管这一现象并非普遍，但从此 “go postal” 就成为了描述某人突然暴怒或失控行为的表达。

definition.en: This phrase comes from the geographical direction, mainly referring to moving south. On a map, south is usually towards the bottom, which metaphorically represents decline or negative changes. In English, "go south" is often used to describe a situation that suddenly deteriorates or becomes uncontrollable, similar to the Chinese expressions “走下坡路” or “每况愈下”.

examples.en: After the new policy was implemented, sales started to go south.
examples.cn: 新政策实施后，销售情况开始变糟。

examples.en: Their relationship began to go south after the argument.
examples.cn: 争吵之后，他们的关系开始恶化。

examples.en: The project was going well, but then it suddenly went south.
examples.cn: 项目进行得很顺利，但突然间就出了问题。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于地理方向，主要是指朝南走。在地图上，南方通常在下方，隐喻着下降和负面变化。在英语中，“go south” 常用来形容情况突然变坏或者事情失控，类似于中文的 “走下坡路” 或 “每况愈下” 的意思。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the New Testament in the Bible, specifically Matthew 5:41, where Jesus said, "If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with them two miles." The meaning behind this is that when you are asked to do something, you should put in extra effort. Today, the idiom is used to describe people who are willing to go beyond the minimum requirement to achieve higher goals or provide better service.

examples.en: She always goes the extra mile to help her students succeed.
examples.cn: 她总是加倍努力帮助她的学生取得成功。

examples.en: Our customer service team goes the extra mile to ensure customer satisfaction.
examples.cn: 我们的客户服务团队总是多做一点，以确保客户满意。

examples.en: I'm so grateful to my colleagues who went the extra mile to complete the project on time.
examples.cn: 我非常感激我的同事们，他们加倍努力按时完成了这个项目。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自《新约圣经》中《马太福音》第五章41节，其中耶稣提到 “有人强逼你走一里路，你就同他走二里”。这句话的意思是，当你被要求完成一些事情时，应该多做一点，多付出一些努力。现在，这个习语常用于表示人们不满足于完成最基本的任务，而是愿意付出额外的努力来达到更高的目标或提供更好的服务。

definition.en: This phrase originates from 19th-century Britain, referring to making the maximum effort in an activity or situation, especially completing the whole process without hesitation, such as eating an entire hog. Over time, this expression has become more general, applying to various pursuits and decisions, meaning to commit fully to something rather than doing it halfway.

examples.en: If we're going to renovate the kitchen, let's go the whole hog and do it properly.
examples.cn: 如果我们要翻新厨房，那就全力以赴，好好做。

examples.en: He's decided to go the whole hog and start his own business.
examples.cn: 他决定一鼓作气，创办自己的公司。

examples.en: Instead of just fixing the leak, they went the whole hog and replaced the entire roof.
examples.cn: 他们没有只是修补漏水，而是全力以赴，更换了整个屋顶。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于十九世纪的英国，指的是在某种活动或情境中投入最大的努力，尤其是毫不犹豫地完成整个过程（例如吃掉整只猪）。随着时间的推移，这个表达变得更为广泛，适用于各种追求和决策场合，意指全心全意地完成某事，而不是半途而废。

title: Go through it with a fine-tooth comb

definition.cn: “仔细检查” 或 “一丝不苟地检查”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from using a fine-tooth comb to groom hair, intending to catch small objects or tangles in the hair. Such combs can capture very small items in the hair, so the phrase has come to mean conducting a very thorough examination or review.

examples.en: The auditor will go through the records with a fine-tooth comb to ensure there are no discrepancies.
examples.cn: 审计员会仔细检查记录，以确保没有差异。

examples.en: She went through the contract with a fine-tooth comb before signing it.
examples.cn: 她在签合同之前仔细地检查了一遍。

examples.en: They need to go through the proposal with a fine-tooth comb before presenting it to the board.
examples.cn: 他们需要在提交给董事会之前仔细审查这个提案。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于使用细齿梳子来梳理头发，目的是捕捉头发中的细小物体或结。这种梳子可以捕捉到头发中非常小的东西，因此这个短语就用来表示非常仔细的检查或审查。

title: Go to hell in a handbasket

definition.en: The exact origin of this phrase is not entirely clear. Some researchers believe it derives from the 18th-century American coal miners who would transport coal in baskets to the surface, and sometimes these baskets would fall into deep pits. Others suggest it comes from folklore about being carried to hell in a basket. Both interpretations convey a rapid and uncontrollable descent into disaster.

examples.en: With the economy collapsing, the whole country's going to hell in a handbasket.
examples.cn: 随着经济崩溃，整个国家正迅速走向毁灭。

examples.en: If we don't address climate change, we are all going to hell in a handbasket.
examples.cn: 如果我们不解决气候变化问题，我们都会迅速走向灭亡。

examples.en: His life went to hell in a handbasket after he lost his job.
examples.cn: 失业之后，他的生活迅速恶化。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源并不完全明确，有些研究者认为它源自18世纪美国的煤矿工人，他们会用手提篮将煤炭运送到地表，而有时这些篮子会直接掉入深坑。另一些解释则认为这个短语起源于旧时传说中，被用篮子送去地狱的人。这两种说法都体现了快速而不可阻挡的下滑和灾难。

definition.en: This idiom originates from the physical act of breaking or falling apart, later being used to describe a person who emotionally or mentally collapses under significant stress or distress. It indicates a person losing emotional control and becoming completely overwhelmed.

examples.en: After hearing the tragic news, she completely went to pieces.
examples.cn: 听到那个悲惨的消息后，她彻底崩溃了。

examples.en: He fell to pieces during the meeting when he couldn't handle the pressure.
examples.cn: 在会议上他无法承受压力时崩溃了。

examples.en: She's usually so strong, but even she went to pieces after her pet passed away.
examples.cn: 她通常很坚强，但在她的宠物去世后，她还是崩溃了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的成语起源于物理上的崩溃或分裂，后被用来形容人在面对巨大压力或困境时情绪或精神上的崩溃。它表示一个人在感情上无法自持，完全失去了冷静和控制。

definition.cn: “走下坡路” 或 “变得很糟糕”。
definition.en: The origin of the phrase is not entirely clear, but it is commonly believed to come from places where, in bad economic or social conditions, people might throw discarded food and useless items to the dogs. "Go to the dogs" means something deteriorates from a good state to a bad one, losing its value like discarded food.

examples.en: After the new management took over, the company went to the dogs.
examples.cn: 新管理层接手后，公司就开始走下坡路了。

examples.en: Many people say the neighborhood has gone to the dogs in recent years.
examples.cn: 很多人说这个社区近年来变得很糟糕。

examples.en: When he stopped caring, his grades went to the dogs.
examples.cn: 当他不再努力学习时，他的成绩就开始走下坡路了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源尚不完全明确，但普遍认为来自于某些经济或社会状况不好的地方，人们可能会把废弃的食物和无用的东西扔给狗狗。“Go to the dogs” 意味着某事物从好的状态变得糟糕，就像被丢弃的食物一样没有价值。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the early American West, where going to town often meant people would engage in spending, socializing, or other significant activities. In modern usage, "go to town" has come to widely mean putting in a lot of effort or doing something very enthusiastically.

examples.en: They really went to town on the decorations for the party.
examples.cn: 他们在派对的装饰上真的下了很大功夫。

examples.en: When she started painting, she went to town on the canvas.
examples.cn: 当她开始画画时，她在画布上大展拳脚。

examples.en: He went to town on that buffet, trying almost everything.
examples.cn: 他在那个自助餐上拼命地吃，几乎尝试了所有的食物。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国早期的西部，当时人们去镇上（主要是指城镇）表明他们要进行消费、社交或其他重要的活动。现代社会中，“go to town” 已广泛用来表示在某个任务或活动上全力以赴，或是极其卖力地做某件事。

definition.cn: “化为乌有” 或 “化为烟雾”。这个短语用来形容计划、希望、努力等突然间失败，或者一切都白费，一切变得徒劳无功。
definition.en: This phrase has its origins in fire. When an object catches fire, it turns into smoke and vanishes completely, symbolizing something that was tangible but has now disappeared. Thus, "go up in smoke" signifies that a hope, plan, or effort has suddenly and completely vanished, just like smoke.

examples.en: All of our hard work went up in smoke after the company decided to cancel the project.
examples.cn: 在公司决定取消项目后，我们的所有努力都化为乌有了。

examples.en: His dreams of traveling the world went up in smoke when he lost all his savings.
examples.cn: 当他丢了所有的积蓄后，他环游世界的梦想也化为乌有了。

examples.en: The celebration plans went up in smoke due to the sudden storm.
examples.cn: 由于突如其来的暴风雨，庆祝计划都化为乌有了。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源与火焰有关。物体着火，会变成烟雾消失殆尽，象征着某种实际存在的东西彻底消失。因此, “go up in smoke” 就表示某种期望或者计划突然完全消失，就像烟雾一样。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the natural flow of water, depicting a state of going along with the current. When applied to human situations, it means not to worry or struggle too much but to adapt to the current circumstances and go along with what is happening. It is suitable when advising someone not to be overly concerned or stressed about something.

examples.en: Instead of planning every detail, sometimes it's best to just go with the flow.
examples.cn: 有时候，不如不要计划每个细节，而是顺其自然。

examples.en: When traveling in a new country, it's often easier to go with the flow.
examples.cn: 在一个新的国家旅行时，通常顺其自然会更容易。

examples.en: I decided to relax and go with the flow during the meeting.
examples.cn: 我决定在会议期间放松，顺其自然。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于自然界的水流，它描绘了顺应流动的状态。用在人们的处境时，它意味着不要过于担忧和抗争，而是顺应当前的局势和环境，自然地跟随其发展。适用于劝说他人不要过于纠结或担忧某事。

definition.cn: “关键人物” 或 “专门负责某事的人”。
definition.en: This phrase is used to describe the most reliable and capable person people turn to in a particular field or situation. It originates from the notion that when faced with problems or challenges, there’s always a specific person who can help, often providing effective solutions, thus becoming the key person or dependable go-to person.

examples.en: When it comes to fixing computers, John is our go-to-guy.
examples.cn: 提到修电脑，约翰是我们的关键人物。

examples.en: Every time we need advice on financial matters, Sarah is our go-to-guy.
examples.cn: 每当我们需要有关财务问题的建议时，萨拉就是我们的专门负责人。

examples.en: Mike is the go-to-guy for organizing any office event.
examples.cn: 组织任何办公室活动，迈克是我们的关键人物。

origin.cn: 这个短语用来形容在某个领域或情况下，人们依赖的那个最可靠、最具能力的人。这种表述源于人们在面对问题或难题时，总会有一个特定的人可以求助，并且这个人通常都能提供有效的解决方案，堪称关键人物或得力干将。

definition.en: This phrase can be traced back to Old English times, meaning that some things are so obvious that they don't need to be said. It's often used to stress that certain matters are common knowledge or self-evident truths.

examples.en: It goes without saying that you should apologize for being late.
examples.cn: 显而易见，你应该为迟到道歉。

examples.en: It goes without saying that you need to study to pass the exam.
examples.cn: 不言而喻，你需要学习才能通过考试。

examples.en: It goes without saying that safety is our top priority.
examples.cn: 不言而喻，安全是我们的首要任务。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古英语时期，意指某些事情如此显然，以至于无需说出来。这个成语常用于强调某些事情是大家都知道的常识或理所当然的真理。

definition.en: This phrase originates from Greek mythology, referring to a period of peace, prosperity, and happiness. It is used to describe a peak period in history for a country, culture, or individual, usually indicating the time when development and achievements reached their zenith.

examples.en: The 1950s are often considered the golden age of American cinema.
examples.cn: 1950 年代常被认为是美国电影的黄金时代。

examples.en: Many believe that the golden age of technology is happening now.
examples.cn: 许多人认为现在是科技的黄金时代。

examples.en: He often reminisces about the golden age of his career in the 1980s.
examples.cn: 他经常怀念20世纪80年代自己职业生涯的黄金时代。

origin.cn: “黄金时代” 这一短语源自于古希腊神话中的一个时期，象征着和平、繁荣和幸福。它被用来描述一个国家、文化或个人在历史上最辉煌的时期，通常意味着一个时代的发展和成就达到了顶峰。

definition.cn: “黄金机会” 或 “千载难逢的机会”。
definition.en: This phrase emphasizes the precious and rare nature of an opportunity. Using "golden" to describe the chance indicates that it is a rare, potentially life-changing opportunity that is highly valuable and worth seizing. Such opportunities do not come by often, hence the term "golden opportunity."

examples.en: This job offer is a golden opportunity you shouldn't miss.
examples.cn: 这个工作机会是一个你不应该错过的黄金机会。

examples.en: Winning the scholarship was a golden opportunity for her education.
examples.cn: 赢得奖学金是她教育生涯中的一个黄金机会。

examples.en: The partnership presented a golden opportunity to expand the business.
examples.cn: 这个合作关系提供了扩展业务的黄金机会。

origin.cn: 这个短语突出了机会的宝贵和稀有。它用 “黄金” 来形容机会，表明这是一个难得的甚至可能是改变人生的机会，非常值得把握。这样的机会并不常有，因此被称为 “golden opportunity”。

definition.en: The origin of this idiom can be traced back to the early 20th century, first appearing in the UK. It is used to describe someone who is good-natured and helpful. Conversely, "bad egg" refers to someone who is not well-behaved and disappointing. Therefore, "good egg" is often used to praise someone with upright and kind character.

examples.en: Tom is such a good egg; he's always willing to help others.
examples.cn: 汤姆真是一个好人；他总是乐于助人。

examples.en: She's a real good egg, always thinking about others before herself.
examples.cn: 她是一个真正的好人，总是先考虑别人。

examples.en: Even in tough times, Jack remained a good egg and stayed honest.
examples.cn: 即使在困难时期，杰克仍然是个好人，保持诚实。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到20世纪初，最早出现在英国。它常用于描述一个品行端正、乐于助人的人。相比之下，“bad egg” 则表示一个品行不佳、令人失望的人。因此，"good egg" 常常用来称赞那些行为和性格都非常正直友善的人。

definition.cn: “对你有好处” 或 “真替你高兴”。
definition.en: This phrase is often used to express approval and encouragement towards someone else's actions, achievements, or decisions. In North America, "Good for you!" is a way to congratulate, commend, or encourage someone, usually employed when the person has achieved something or made a positive choice.

examples.en: You got the promotion? Good for you!
examples.cn: 你升职了？真替你高兴！

examples.en: You finally finished your degree? Good for you!
examples.cn: 你终于完成学业了？真替你开心！

examples.en: You quit smoking? Good for you!
examples.cn: 你戒烟了？对你有好处！

origin.cn: 这个短语常用于表达对他人表现、成就或决定的认可和鼓励。在北美，"Good for you!" 是一种表示祝贺、赞许或鼓励的话语，通常用于对方取得成就或做出积极决定时。

definition.cn: “总算摆脱了” 或 “幸好走了”。
definition.en: This phrase originated from Middle English "riddance," which means clearing or getting rid of something. It conveys the feeling of relief when an undesirable or unpleasant person or thing is gone, often used to express one's gladness about such a departure.

examples.en: When he finally quit, everyone in the office thought, good riddance.
examples.cn: 当他终于辞职时，办公室里的每个人都觉得：总算摆脱了。

examples.en: They moved out yesterday, and I say good riddance. They were terrible neighbors.
examples.cn: 他们昨天搬走了，我觉得幸好走了。他们是糟糕的邻居。

examples.en: Good riddance to that old car; it was nothing but trouble.
examples.cn: 总算摆脱了那辆旧车；它一直带来麻烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于中世纪的英国英语 "riddance"，意为清除或摆脱。表达的意思是希望坏事或令人不快的事物尽快从自己身边消失，通常用于谈论自己不喜欢或厌恶的人或事离开时的一种解脱感。

title: Good things come to those who wait

definition.cn: “好事多磨” 或 “耐心等待终有好结果”。
definition.en: This phrase can trace its origins to ancient wisdom and proverbs, highlighting the importance of patience and waiting. In modern society, it is often used to encourage people to stay patient in the pursuit of success or goals, implying that good things take time to materialize.

examples.en: Despite the struggles, she believes that good things come to those who wait.
examples.cn: 尽管有很多困难，她仍然相信好事多磨。

examples.en: Good things come to those who wait, so be patient.
examples.cn: 好事多磨，所以要有耐心。

examples.en: He finally got the promotion after years of hard work, proving that good things come to those who wait.
examples.cn: 经过多年的努力，他终于得到了晋升，证明了好事多磨。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古老的智慧和谚语，强调耐心和等待的重要性。在现代社会，通常用于鼓励人们在追求成功或目标的过程中保持耐心，不要急于求成。通俗说法即是：美好的事物需要时间来实现。

definition.en: This phrase is used to acknowledge that some information or news is useful or interesting. It is commonly used to show appreciation for the information provided or to confirm its importance. This expression is rather informal and is suitable for everyday conversations.

examples.en: "There's a new coffee shop opening down the street." "Oh, good to know."
examples.cn: “街上有一家新的咖啡馆开张。” “哦，知道了。”

examples.en: "The meeting has been moved to 3 PM." "Thanks for the update, good to know."
examples.cn: “会议改到下午3点了。” “谢谢通知，好知道。”

examples.en: "You can get a discount if you order online." "Really? Good to know!"
examples.cn: “如果你在网上订购可以有折扣。” “真的吗？好知道！”

origin.cn: 这个短语用来表示某些信息或消息有用或者感兴趣。通常用于对他人提供的信息表示感谢或确认其重要性。这种表达比较随意、口语化，适用于日常交流中。

definition.cn: “哇哦，太棒了！” 或 “真是令人兴奋！”
definition.en: This phrase originates from the candy "gumdrops" that children often enjoy in English-speaking countries. The word "Goody" is derived from "good" and conveys excitement and a celebratory tone. It is typically used to express strong pleasure and delight, similar to saying "great" or "fantastic" in Chinese.

examples.en: “Goody, goody gumdrops!” she exclaimed when she saw the surprise party.
examples.cn: 当她看到惊喜派对时，她喊道：“哇哦，太棒了！”

examples.en: The kids shouted, “Goody, goody gumdrops!” when they found out they were going to the amusement park.
examples.cn: 孩子们在得知要去游乐园时大喊：“哇哦，太棒了！”

examples.en: “Goody, goody gumdrops!” John yelled as he opened his birthday present.
examples.cn: 约翰在打开生日礼物时喊道：“哇哦，太棒了！”

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于英语国家儿童经常吃的糖果 “橡皮糖”（gumdrops），而 “Goody” 一词则源自 “good”，带有兴奋和庆祝意味。它通常用来表达强烈的喜悦和兴奋，类似于中文中的 “太棒了” 或 “好极了”。

definition.en: This phrase originates from American slang, first used in the early 20th century. "Goof" means a foolish mistake or behavior, while "off" implies getting rid of or quitting. Thus, "goof off" refers to someone wasting time or not doing what they should be doing. This idiom is commonly used in informal settings, especially when discussing work or study to describe not being serious or committed.

examples.en: Instead of doing his homework, he spent the entire afternoon goofing off.
examples.cn: 他没有做作业，整个下午都在偷懒。

examples.en: The boss caught them goofing off on company time.
examples.cn: 老板抓到他们在上班时间偷懒。

examples.en: You can't expect to pass the exam if you keep goofing off in class.
examples.cn: 如果你在课堂上一直偷懒，别指望能通过考试。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国俚语，最早在20世纪初使用。“Goof” 表示愚蠢的错误或行为，而 “off” 则表示摆脱或离开。因此，“goof off” 指的是某人无所事事、浪费时间，通常是在应该做某事的时候。这个短语在非正式场合中较为常用，尤其在谈论工作或学习时形容不认真或不投入。

definition.cn: “未受任何惩罚” 或 “逃脱惩罚”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the Old English word “scot,” which referred to a tax or payment. In medieval times, "scot" was a term used for a kind of tax that indicated some form of share. If someone “got off scot-free,” it meant they avoided this tax or responsibility. Over time, it evolved to mean avoiding any form of punishment or burden.

examples.en: He broke the vase but got off scot-free because no one saw him.
examples.cn: 他打碎了花瓶，但因为没有人看到他，所以他逃脱了惩罚。

examples.en: Despite the evidence, the suspect got off scot-free due to a technicality.
examples.cn: 尽管有证据，由于程序问题，嫌疑人还是未受任何惩罚。

examples.en: It's not fair that he got off scot-free while we had to bear the consequences.
examples.cn: 他逃脱了惩罚，而我们却不得不承担后果，这不公平。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于古英语中的 “scot”，意为税收或款项。在中世纪，"scot" 是另一种税，指的是某种分摊费用。如果某人 “got off scot-free”，意味着他们逃脱了这种税务或责任，最终这一说法演变为逃避任何形式的惩罚或负担。

definition.cn: “被严厉盘问” 或 “受到严格的审问”。
definition.en: In origins dating back to the late 19th century, the phrase "the third degree" was associated with a tough level of interrogation or coercion by police. The "third degree" might come from the Masonic system of degrees, where the third degree signifies a high level requiring rigorous testing. Over time, the phrase morphed into common usage to describe scenarios where someone is subjected to intense questioning.

examples.en: He got the third degree from his parents after coming home late.
examples.cn: 他回家晚了以后被父母严厉盘问。

examples.en: After the accident, the police gave her the third degree about what happened.
examples.cn: 事故发生后，警察对她进行了严厉的盘问，询问发生了什么。

examples.en: I felt like I got the third degree when my boss questioned me about the project's delay.
examples.cn: 当我的老板质问项目延迟的情况时，我感觉自己受到了严厉的盘问。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到十九世纪末。当时，警察用 “三度逼供法”（the third degree）来指严厉的审问或逼供。“第三度” 可能源于共济会等级制度，在共济会里，第三度是一个相当高的等级，代表了严格的考验和衡量。随着时间的推移，这个短语便演变为描述受到严厉盘问的情景。

definition.en: This phrase originates from animals such as dogs or cats that have hackles (the hairs on the back of their neck). When these animals feel threatened or angry, their hackles rise as a sign of aggression. Thus, this expression is used to describe someone who is angry or provoked by something.

examples.en: The new policy really got their hackles up.
examples.cn: 这项新政策真的让他们很生气。

examples.en: The comment he made got her hackles up immediately.
examples.cn: 他的话立刻激怒了她。

examples.en: You can tell when he gets his hackles up by the way he clenches his fists.
examples.cn: 你可以从他握紧拳头的方式看出他什么时候生气了。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于狗或猫等带有脊毛的动物，当它们受到威胁或感到愤怒时，脊毛会竖起来以示威胁。因此，这个表达用来描述某人因为某件事情而感到愤怒或被激怒。

definition.cn: “抓住救命稻草” 或 “孤注一掷”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from an old metaphor where a drowning person, in a desperate attempt to survive, would grasp at even a straw, having no other options. In modern usage, it describes situations where someone in extreme or desperate circumstances attempts any means they can, even if these means are likely to be ineffective.

examples.en: In his search for a cure, he was grasping at straws by trying various unproven remedies.
examples.cn: 为了寻找一种治愈方法，他尝试各种未经证明的疗法，真的是在抓住救命稻草。

examples.en: With no real evidence, the detective felt like he was just grasping at straws.
examples.cn: 没有确凿的证据，那位侦探感觉自己不过是在抓住救命稻草。

examples.en: He knew the job was almost impossible, but he kept grasping at straws in hopes of success.
examples.cn: 他知道这份工作几乎是不可能完成的，但他依然抓住救命稻草，希望能成功。

origin.cn: 这个成语起源于古代的一个比喻，指溺水的人为了求生，即使是一根稻草也会抓住，因为他们没有别的选择。在现代，这个成语用来形容人在极端或绝望的情况下，为了生存或成功而尝试任何一线希望或采取任何措施，尽管这些措施可能无效。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the 19th century to describe work shifts that occur during the late-night or early morning hours. Because this time period is typically very quiet and dark, akin to the atmosphere of a graveyard, it became known as the "graveyard shift".

examples.en: He’s working the graveyard shift at the hospital this week.
examples.cn: 他这周在医院上夜班。

examples.en: It’s hard to adjust to the graveyard shift because of the sleep schedule.
examples.cn: 由于睡眠时间安排，适应夜班是很难的。

examples.en: The factory runs 24/7, so someone always needs to cover the graveyard shift.
examples.cn: 工厂全天运行，所以总是需要有人值夜班。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于19世纪，用于形容在深夜或者清晨时段工作的班次。因为这个时段往往非常安静、黑暗，与墓地（graveyard）的氛围相似，因此被称为 “墓地班次” 或 “凌晨班”。

definition.cn: “肥差” 或 “轻松赚钱的工作”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in the American railroad industry in the early 20th century. Railroad workers made more money on certain routes and the work was easier, so they referred to these routes as "gravy." Over time, "gravy train" has come to describe any situation or job where people make money easily.

examples.en: He's been riding the gravy train ever since he landed that high-paying government contract.
examples.cn: 自从他拿到那个高薪的政府合同后，他就一直在享受肥差。

examples.en: Many believe that working in the tech industry is a gravy train these days.
examples.cn: 许多人认为如今在科技行业工作是一份肥差。

examples.en: Investors often look for startups that can become their next gravy train.
examples.cn: 投资者常常寻找能成为他们下一个 “肥差” 的创业公司。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于20世纪的美国铁路行业。铁路员工在某些线路上工作时比其他线路赚钱更多，而且工作也更轻松。人们就用 “gravy”（调味肉汁，象征财富）来形容这些特别赚钱的线路。随着时间的推移，“gravy train” 被广泛用来描述任何让人轻松挣钱的情况或职位。

definition.cn: “灰色地带” 或 “模棱两可的区域”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from legal terminology, used to describe areas or situations that are not clearly defined by law. These matters are often difficult to categorize or resolve. In modern contexts, "gray area" is widely used to refer to situations that are ambiguous, unclear, or hard to make definitive judgments about.

examples.en: The legality of that business practice exists in a gray area.
examples.cn: 那种商业行为的合法性存在于灰色地带。

examples.en: There's a gray area in our policy about social media use at work.
examples.cn: 我们的政策中关于工作时使用社交媒体有一个模棱两可的区域。

examples.en: Intellectual property law can often be a gray area.
examples.cn: 知识产权法往往可以是一个灰色地带。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于法律术语，用来描述那些没有明确法律规定的领域或情况，这些事情通常不清楚如何归类或处理。在现代语境中，"gray area" 被广泛用于指代不明确、不清晰或难以做出明确判断的情况。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the workers in mechanical repair shops, who often come into contact with a lot of lubricants and grease. The combination of "grease" and "monkey" is used to describe these workers. Though somewhat slangy, it frequently refers to people who are skilled in fixing machinery, particularly car mechanics.

examples.en: My brother is a grease monkey at the local garage.
examples.cn: 我哥哥是本地车库的修车工。

examples.en: The grease monkey fixed my car in no time.
examples.cn: 那个修车工很快就把我的车修好了。

examples.en: He's been working as a grease monkey since he finished high school.
examples.cn: 他自从高中毕业后就一直在当修车工。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于那些在机械维修车间工作的工人，他们通常会接触到大量的润滑油和油脂，因此 “grease” (油脂) 和 “monkey” (猴子) 的组合用来形容这些人。尽管这个词有些俚语化，但它经常用于表示那些擅长修理机械的人，特别是汽车维修工。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the 19th century, meaning even faster than ordinary lightning. During that time, people would use grease or oil to lubricate their carriages, making them run smoother and faster on muddy roads. Hence, "greased lightning" came to describe anything exceedingly fast or efficient.

examples.en: He finished the task like greased lightning.
examples.cn: 他完成任务的速度快如闪电。

examples.en: The new processor runs the software like greased lightning.
examples.cn: 新处理器运行软件的速度非常快。

examples.en: She zipped through the crowd like greased lightning to catch the train.
examples.cn: 她快如闪电地穿过人群赶上了火车。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于19世纪，意思是比普通的闪电更快。在那个时期，人们会用油脂或油来润滑马车，使它们能在泥泞的道路上行驶得更顺畅、更快。于是，“greased lightning” 就被用来形容任何非常快速或高效的事情。

definition.en: This idiom traces back to the Greek philosopher Aristotle's notion. When two intelligent people think alike, share the same opinion, or make the same decision, we use this phrase to commend them. This saying is used to highlight that reaching the same conclusions or taking similar actions as others is a sign of intelligence and wisdom.

examples.en: "I was just about to suggest the same thing!" "Well, great minds think alike!"
examples.cn: “我正准备提同样的建议呢！” “嗯，英雄所见略同！”

examples.en: Both of us brought the same book to the meeting. Great minds think alike.
examples.cn: 我们两个都带了同一本书来开会。英雄所见略同。

examples.en: When we presented our ideas, they were almost identical. Great minds think alike.
examples.cn: 当我们展示我们的想法时，它们几乎完全一样。英雄所见略同。

origin.cn: 这个成语的来历可以追溯到古希腊哲学家亚里士多德的理念。当两个聪明人思想一致、意见相同或做出一样的决定时，我们会用这句短语来赞赏。这句话用来指出，与别人得出相同的结论或采取相同的行动，是一种高智商和智慧的表象。

definition.cn: “脸色苍白” 或 “看起来病恹恹的”。
definition.en: This phrase originated with sailors and seafarers who often felt seasick, resulting in them having a pale or greenish complexion. Over time, this expression has become widely used to describe anyone who feels physically unwell or sick.

examples.en: He looked green around the gills after the roller coaster ride.
examples.cn: 坐过山车后，他看起来脸色苍白。

examples.en: She was green around the gills during the flight due to turbulence.
examples.cn: 由于气流的影响，她在飞行中脸色发白。

examples.en: After drinking too much last night, he felt green around the gills this morning.
examples.cn: 昨晚喝多了之后，他今天早上感觉很不舒服。

origin.cn: 这个短语的来历与船员和水手有关，他们在海上工作时往往会因为晕船而感到不适，脸色因此变得苍白或发绿。后来，这个表达被广泛用于描述任何在身体上感到不适或生病的人。

definition.cn: “绿色房间” 或 “演员休息室”。
definition.en: This phrase originates in the theatre and entertainment industry, referring to a room where performers wait and relax before their performance. It is said that in the Elizabethan era, theatre walls in these rooms were often painted green to reduce eye strain for actors. In modern usage, the "green room" typically refers to a waiting and preparation room for actors and artists in television, theater, and film settings.

examples.en: The actors chatted with each other in the green room before the show.
examples.cn: 演员们在演出前在绿色房间里互相聊天。

examples.en: She was so nervous that she almost fainted in the green room.
examples.cn: 她太紧张了，差点在绿色房间里晕倒。

examples.en: The director visited the green room to give last-minute instructions.
examples.cn: 导演到绿色房间去做最后的指示。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于戏剧和娱乐行业，指的是演职人员在表演之前待命和放松的休息室。据说在伊丽莎白时代，剧院的休息室墙壁常刷成绿色，以减轻演员眼疲劳。现代使用中，"green room" 主要指电视、戏剧、电影拍摄现场供演员、艺术家候场和准备的休息室。

definition.cn: “园艺高手” 或 “非常擅长种植植物的人”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from those who have exceptional gardening skills, as their fingers are always "colored green" from handling plants. Having a "green thumb" means you have the ability to make plants grow healthily and thrive. It is usually used to describe someone who excels in gardening.

examples.en: She must have a green thumb because her garden is always full of beautiful flowers.
examples.cn: 她一定是个园艺高手，因为她的花园总是开满了美丽的花朵。

examples.en: My grandfather has a green thumb; he can turn any barren land into a lush garden.
examples.cn: 我爷爷是个园艺高手；他能把任何一片贫瘠的土地变成郁郁葱葱的花园。

examples.en: Even though I don't have a green thumb, I enjoy trying to grow plants in my spare time.
examples.cn: 即使我不是园艺高手，我还是喜欢在空闲时间尝试种植植物。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于那些具备特别好的园艺技能的人，因为他们的手指总是被植物的绿色给染上了。拥有 “green thumb” 意味着你有能力使植物健康茂盛地生长，通常用来形容一个在园艺方面表现特别出色的人。

definition.cn: “咬牙坚持” 或 “强颜欢笑面对困境”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the show of resilience, remaining smiling while enduring an unpleasant or painful situation. Although the precise origin is unclear, it is often used to advise people to endure and face difficulties that cannot be immediately changed.

examples.en: Even though the project was stressful, he chose to grin and bear it until it was completed.
examples.cn: 尽管这个项目让人很有压力，他还是选择咬牙坚持，直到完成。

examples.en: She didn’t like her new boss, but she decided to grin and bear it for the sake of her career.
examples.cn: 她不喜欢她的新老板，但为了她的事业，她决定强颜欢笑面对。

examples.en: Sometimes you just have to grin and bear it when things don’t go your way.
examples.cn: 有时候，当事情不按你预期发展时，你只能咬牙坚持。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于一种韧性的表现，当面对令自己不悦或痛苦的情况时，保持微笑并坚持下去。虽然具体的起源不太明确，但它通常用于建议人们在面对无法立即改变的困境时，选择忍耐和坚强面对。

definition.en: This idiom originates from the historical use of guinea pigs in scientific research and experiments. Over time, the phrase has evolved to refer to any person or thing that is used as a subject for experimentation or testing.

examples.en: They used me as a guinea pig for their new training program.
examples.cn: 他们把我当作他们新培训计划的小白鼠。

examples.en: I don't want to be the guinea pig for this new medication.
examples.cn: 我不想成为这种新药物的试验对象。

examples.en: She volunteered to be the guinea pig for the experiment.
examples.cn: 她自愿成为这个实验的小白鼠。

origin.cn: “Guinea pig” 原指豚鼠，这种小动物常用于科学研究和实验，因此在英语中，这个短语逐渐延伸为指代某人或某物被用作试验或测试的对象。 这个短语源自于豚鼠作为实验动物的历史。在科学实验中，豚鼠常被用来进行各种医学和心理研究，因此 “Guinea pig” 自然衍生出了 “试验对象” 的意思，通常用来形容某人为某些新事物或新方法进行尝试或测试。

definition.en: Originating from the Chinese term "工合," which means "work together" or "cooperate," "gung ho" was adopted by the U.S. Marine Corps during World War II to describe high enthusiasm and teamwork. Over time, it has become a colloquial expression in American English, denoting someone who is extremely eager and enthusiastic, especially about work or a particular mission.

examples.en: He's so gung ho about the new project, it’s contagious.
examples.cn: 他对这个新项目充满干劲，这种热情是会传染的。

examples.en: The new manager is really gung ho about improving our team’s performance.
examples.cn: 新经理对提升我们团队的表现充满热情。

examples.en: While she’s gung ho about working late, not everyone shares her enthusiasm.
examples.cn: 虽然她非常干劲十足地加班，但不是所有人都和她一样热情。

origin.cn: “Gung ho” 是美国海军陆战队从中文的 “工合” 一词中借用来的，意思是 “工作互助”。在第二次世界大战期间，驻扎在中国的美军采纳了这个词来形容高度的积极性和合作精神。后来，这个短语在美式英语中广泛传播，表示一个人尽心尽力、热情高涨地投入工作或某项任务。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the instinctive response people have towards situations, unrelated to logical thinking. The "gut" refers to an internal sensation often felt in the abdomen during stress or anxiety. This sensation is considered a primitive and quick reaction mechanism, helping us make decisions when there isn't enough time for logical analysis.

examples.en: I had a gut feeling that something was wrong.
examples.cn: 我有一种直觉，感觉有些不对劲。

examples.en: She trusted her gut feeling and avoided the deal.
examples.cn: 她相信她的直觉，避开了这笔交易。

examples.en: Sometimes, you just have to go with your gut feeling.
examples.cn: 有时候，你只能跟随你的直觉。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于人们对事物的本能反应，与逻辑思考无关。“Gut”（肠胃）指的是一种内脏的感觉，在压力或紧张时，人们常常会感受到腹部的不适。这种感觉被认为是一种原始的、快速的反应机制，它帮助我们在没有足够时间进行逻辑分析时做出决定。

definition.cn: “以毒攻毒” 或 “用少量酒解宿醉”。
definition.en: The full phrase "hair of the dog that bit you" originates from an old medical practice where people believed using the hair of the dog that bit them could cure the bite wound. Similarly, in modern society, it is used to describe the practice of drinking a small amount of alcohol to alleviate or cure a hangover caused by excessive drinking.

examples.en: He had a bad hangover, so he decided to have a hair of the dog in the morning.
examples.cn: 他宿醉很严重，所以他决定早上喝一点酒以毒攻毒。

examples.en: She claims that a hair of the dog helps her recover after a long night of drinking.
examples.cn: 她声称少量酒能帮助她在一夜痛饮后恢复过来。

examples.en: Many people swear by a hair of the dog as a hangover cure.
examples.cn: 很多人发誓用少量酒作为治宿醉的疗法很有效。

origin.cn: 这个短语的完整形式是 "hair of the dog that bit you"，起源于古老的医学实践，人们相信用咬过人的狗的毛来治疗狗咬伤的部位。同样地，现代社会中，人们用该短语来描述用少量的酒来减轻或治愈因饮酒过度引起的宿醉症状。

definition.cn: “毫厘之差” 或者 “极窄的距离”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the unit of measurement— the width of a hair, meaning a very small distance or difference. This expression is often used to describe situations that are extremely close or narrowly avoided.

examples.en: The car missed the pedestrian by a hair's breadth.
examples.cn: 那辆车以毫厘之差躲过了行人。

examples.en: He escaped the accident by a hair's breadth.
examples.cn: 他以毫厘之差逃过了这次事故。

examples.en: The negotiations failed by a hair's breadth.
examples.cn: 谈判以毫厘之差失败了。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于测量单位——头发的宽度，意思是非常微小的距离或者差别。这个表达方式常用以描述极其接近或者险些发生的情况。

title: Half a mind to do something

definition.en: This idiom originates from the 19th century and is used to express that someone has an inclination or a mild desire to do something, but is not fully committed or sure about it. It often conveys a sense of hesitation or uncertainty.

examples.en: I have half a mind to quit my job and travel the world.
examples.cn: 我有点想辞掉工作去环游世界。

examples.en: She has half a mind to tell her boss off, but she won't.
examples.cn: 她有点想训斥她的老板，但她不会这么做。

examples.en: He has half a mind to buy that car, but he's still thinking about it.
examples.cn: 他有点想买那辆车，但他还在考虑。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于19世纪，用来表达某个人对做某件事情有不全坚定的意愿，即并不是很有把握或是完全确定要去做，而只是有这个想法。这个表达多用于表达一种犹豫不决的态度。

definition.cn: “事半功倍” 或 “成功的一半”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from combat or warfare strategy. It signifies that if the most challenging or crucial part of a task has been accomplished, then the remaining part will be relatively easy. In modern society, this idiom is commonly used to describe situations where overcoming the main obstacles or key steps makes the remaining tasks easier.

examples.en: Understanding the problem is half the battle.
examples.cn: 理解问题就已经成功了一半。

examples.en: Finding the right tools for the job is half the battle.
examples.cn: 找到合适的工具就已经事半功倍了。

examples.en: Convincing the team of the project's importance is half the battle.
examples.cn: 让团队认识到项目的重要性就已经成功了一半。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于战斗或战争中的策略。它表示，某项任务如果已经完成了最困难或最关键的部分，那么剩余的部分将会相对容易。现代社会中，这个短语常用于描述克服了主要障碍和难题，完成了关键步骤，从而剩下的任务变得容易的情形。

definition.cn: “未经深思熟虑的” 或 “不成熟的”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from cooking, meaning food that is not fully baked or only half-baked. Similarly, when an idea or plan is called "half-baked," it means that it has not been fully thought through or prepared, and is therefore immature or incomplete.

examples.en: He came up with a half-baked scheme to start a business without any market research.
examples.cn: 他提出了一个未经市场研究的、不成熟的商业计划。

examples.en: Her half-baked solutions won't solve the problem.
examples.cn: 她那不成熟的解决方案无法解决问题。

examples.en: We need a well-thought-out plan, not some half-baked idea.
examples.cn: 我们需要一个深思熟虑的计划，而不是一些未经过深思熟虑的想法。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自烹饪术语，意为食物未煮熟或者只煮了一半。同样地，当一个想法或计划被认为是 “*half-baked*”，意味着它没有经过充分思考或准备，不够成熟或完善。

definition.cn: “敲定一个交易” 或 “达成协议”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the process of hammering in metallurgy, implying that through repeated efforts and discussions, a satisfactory agreement is eventually reached. It is often used to describe the negotiation process where parties engage in back-and-forth discussions and compromises to finalize the details and establish a cooperative relationship.

examples.en: After weeks of negotiation, the two companies finally hammered out a deal.
examples.cn: 经过数周的谈判，这两家公司终于敲定了协议。

examples.en: The legal team is working hard to hammer out a deal that satisfies both parties.
examples.cn: 法律团队正在努力敲定一个能令双方都满意的协议。

examples.en: It took months, but we eventually hammered out a deal with our overseas partners.
examples.cn: 花了几个月的时间，但我们最终与海外合作伙伴达成了协议。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于冶金中的锤炼过程，意指通过反复的努力和讨论，最终达成一个满意的协议。通常用于描述在谈判过程中，经过多次磋商和妥协，最终确定细节并达成合作关系。

definition.en: This phrase first appeared in the context of British hunting, where hunters would wear gloves and tie them closely to the falcon's feet. Hence, "Hand in glove" vividly represents a close relationship and coordinated co-operation. Nowadays, this idiom is commonly used to describe a close working relationship between two people or organizations.

examples.en: The manager and the team lead are working hand in glove to improve the project.
examples.cn: 经理和团队负责人正在密切合作以改进项目。

examples.en: Those two companies have been operating hand in glove for years.
examples.cn: 这两家公司已经密切合作多年。

examples.en: Politicians often work hand in glove with lobbyists.
examples.cn: 政客们通常与游说者密切合作。

origin.cn: 这个短语最早出现在英国的狩猎中，狩猎时猎人会在手上戴上手套，并将手套和猎隼的脚紧紧绑定在一起。因此，"Hand in glove" 形象地表示两者之间的密切关系和协调合作。如今，这个短语通常用来描述两个人或两个组织之间的紧密合作关系。

definition.cn: “迅速且大量地” 或 “快速获利”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from a nautical term describing the action of sailors quickly climbing a rope hand over hand. It was later extended to mean acquiring or losing something rapidly, especially in the context of making quick profits or experiencing quick losses.

examples.en: The new product was a hit and the company started making money hand over fist.
examples.cn: 新产品大获成功，公司迅速开始赚钱。

examples.en: They've been losing customers hand over fist since their service declined.
examples.cn: 自从服务质量下降后，他们迅速失去了大量顾客。

examples.en: Investors are profiting hand over fist from the booming stock market.
examples.cn: 投资者们从繁荣的股市中迅速获利。

origin.cn: 这个成语最早源自航海术语，形容船员快速地沿着绳子往上爬时的手部动作，看起来就像手一个接一个地抓住绳子。后来，这个成语被延伸为迅速地获得或失去某些东西，尤其指快速获利或快速亏损。

definition.en: This phrase is typically used to encourage someone not to give up when facing difficulties or challenges. It originates from rock climbing terminology, meaning to hold on tightly and maintain one's position even during the most challenging times. As an idiom, "hang in there" expresses persistence, resilience, and endurance.

examples.en: I know the exam is tough, but hang in there; you'll do great.
examples.cn: 我知道考试很难，但坚持住；你会表现得很好的。

examples.en: This project has been challenging, but let's hang in there and finish it strong.
examples.cn: 这个项目一直很有挑战性，但让我们坚持住，强势完成它。

examples.en: Life can be tough sometimes; just hang in there and things will get better.
examples.cn: 生活有时会很艰难；只要坚持住，事情会变好的。

origin.cn: 这个短语通常用于鼓励一个人在面对困难或挑战时不要放弃。它源于攀岩运动中的术语，表示即使在最困难的时刻也要抓紧并保持自己的位置。作为一个成语，"hang in there" 表达了继续努力、保持坚韧和忍耐的精神。

definition.en: This idiom comes from the idea of holding on tightly, often used to encourage someone to be patient or stay calm. In situations requiring waiting or enduring, it emphasizes the need for patience and suggests that things will improve.

examples.en: Hang tight, the doctor will be with you shortly.
examples.cn: 稍安勿躁，医生很快就会来。

examples.en: Hang tight, I'll be right back.
examples.cn: 稍等一下，我马上回来。

examples.en: Just hang tight, everything will be okay.
examples.cn: 耐心点，一切都会好的。

origin.cn: “Hang tight” 是一个口语化的短语，源自 “紧紧抓住” 的概念，常用于鼓励别人保持耐心或冷静。在面对需要等待或忍耐的情况时，这个短语强调了要有耐心，并暗示情况会有所改善。

definition.en: This phrase originates from early English, with the literal meaning of "happy with whatever luck comes". It primarily describes individuals who are carefree and do not worry much about the future. These people tend to maintain a positive, go-with-the-flow attitude towards life.

examples.en: She's always been a happy-go-lucky person, never worrying too much about what tomorrow brings.
examples.cn: 她一直是个乐天派，从不为明天的事情担忧。

examples.en: His happy-go-lucky nature makes him a joy to be around.
examples.cn: 他那种无忧无虑的性格让人很愿意与他相处。

examples.en: Even in difficult times, she remains happy-go-lucky and optimistic.
examples.cn: 即使在艰难时期，她依旧保持着乐天的心态和乐观的态度。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于早期的英语，它的意思字面上是 “遇事开心”。这个成语主要用来形容那些轻松愉快、不太在意未来的人。他们往往保持积极、随遇而安的生活态度，不因为未来而担忧。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the sales industry, describing a situation where a salesperson uses high-pressure tactics to force or aggressively encourage a consumer to buy a product or service. Unlike the more subtle "soft sell," a hard sell often leaves the consumer feeling uncomfortable or annoyed.

examples.en: The car salesman was giving me a hard sell on the latest model.
examples.cn: 那位汽车销售员拼命向我推销最新款的车型。

examples.en: I don't like when phone companies do a hard sell on their plans.
examples.cn: 我不喜欢电话公司拼命推销他们的套餐计划。

examples.en: Sometimes a hard sell approach can backfire and drive customers away.
examples.cn: 有时候，强行推销的方式可能会适得其反，把顾客吓跑。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于销售领域，指的是销售人员通过施加压力、穷追猛打的方式迫使消费者购买产品或服务。不同于更为柔和的 “软推销”，“强行推销” 通常会让消费者感到不舒服甚至厌烦。

definition.cn: “难以接受的事实” 或 “痛苦的现实”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the experience of taking medication; some pills are hard to swallow not just because of their bitter taste but also because people might be reluctant to accept their need for medication to get better. In modern language, "hard/bitter pill to swallow" corresponds to facing an unpleasant or difficult fact, emphasizing its painfulness or difficulty.

examples.en: Losing the championship game was a hard pill to swallow for the team.
examples.cn: 对团队来说，输掉冠军赛是一个难以接受的事实。

examples.en: It's a bitter pill to swallow knowing that all our efforts were in vain.
examples.cn: 得知我们的所有努力都白费了，这是一个痛苦的现实。

examples.en: The news of the company's bankruptcy was a hard pill to swallow for its employees.
examples.cn: 公司破产的消息对员工们来说是一个难以接受的事实。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于吃药的体验，有些药片难以下咽，不仅因为它们苦涩的味道，还因为人们可能不愿意承认他们需要药物来恢复健康。在现代语言中，“hard/bitter pill to swallow” 对应于面对某个令人不快或难以接受的事实，强调其痛苦或困难。

definition.en: The idiom "Haste makes waste" means that rushing through tasks often leads to mistakes and inefficiencies, ultimately wasting more time and resources. It underscores the importance of doing things carefully and thoroughly, rather than hurrying through them.

examples.en: Don't rush through your homework; remember, haste makes waste.
examples.cn: 不要匆忙做完你的作业；记住，欲速则不达。

examples.en: We learned the hard way that haste makes waste when we built that shed.
examples.cn: 当我们建那个棚子时，我们通过惨痛的教训了解到，欲速则不达。

examples.en: Haste makes waste, so let's take our time and do this right.
examples.cn: 欲速则不达，所以我们要慢慢来，把这件事做对。

origin.cn: 这个成语在英文中的字面意思是 “匆忙导致浪费”。它起源于古老的谚语，提醒人们在急于完成任务时很有可能会因为疏忽或错误而浪费更多时间和资源。因此，该表达强调做事应耐心细致，而不是急于求成。

definition.en: This phrase originates from an 18th-century story told by American politician and writer Benjamin Franklin. In the story, a crafty neighbor manipulates him into helping with an axe under false pretenses. The phrase has evolved to mean that someone has a hidden agenda or personal motive, often when trying to manipulate others.

examples.en: Be careful when talking to him; he always seems to have an axe to grind.
examples.cn: 与他说话时要小心，他似乎总是别有用心。

examples.en: I think she is criticising you because she has an axe to grind.
examples.cn: 我觉得她批评你是因为她心怀不满。

examples.en: It's clear he has an axe to grind against the new policies.
examples.cn: 很明显他对新政策心怀芥蒂。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于18世纪美国政治家和作家Benjamin Franklin，他在一篇文章中描述了一位狡猾的邻居如何利用他来磨斧头。这个短语后来引申为某人怀有隐藏的动机或私心，通常是在试图操纵他人时使用。

definition.cn: “头脑不清楚” 或 “行为古怪”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the imagery of bats in a belfry (a church tower). When there are bats flying around in a belfry, it creates a sense of disorder and confusion. Similarly, having "bats in one's belfry" implies that someone's mind is in disarray or that they are eccentric. It is used to describe someone who behaves unusually or whose thoughts are jumbled.

examples.en: People say he's got bats in his belfry because of his strange inventions.
examples.cn: 人们说他脑子有问题，因为他的发明都很古怪。

examples.en: Don't mind her; she's got bats in her belfry sometimes.
examples.cn: 别在意她；她有时会显得有点怪异。

examples.en: That guy has bats in his belfry if he thinks he can run a marathon without training.
examples.cn: 如果那个人认为自己不用训练就能跑马拉松，那他真是脑子不清楚。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到古老的钟楼（belfry），钟楼的顶部常常会有一些做巢的蝙蝠。如果钟楼内有蝙蝠飞来飞去，整个钟楼就会显得混乱和不协调，比喻一个人的头脑里面也如同有一些蝙蝠飞来飞去那样，神智不清或行为怪异。那么，这个习语通常用来描述一个人行为不寻常或思维不清晰。

definition.cn: “要付出惨痛代价” 或 “要受到严厉的惩罚”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the concept of "hell," which represents extreme consequences or great suffering. It is typically used to indicate that someone will face severe repercussions if they do something wrong or fail to follow the rules.

examples.en: If he finds out you broke his favorite vase, you'll have hell to pay.
examples.cn: 如果他发现你打破了他最喜欢的花瓶，你会付出惨痛代价。

examples.en: You will have hell to pay if you don't finish this project on time.
examples.cn: 如果你没有按时完成这个项目，你会受到严厉的惩罚。

examples.en: There will be hell to pay if they catch you cheating on the exam.
examples.cn: 如果他们抓到你考试作弊，你会有大麻烦。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于 “地狱” 的概念，象征着极其严重的后果或巨大的困苦。这个 idiom 通常用于描述某人如果做错事或者没有遵守规则，将会面临非常严重的后果。

definition.cn: “彻底掌握某事” 或 “对某事驾轻就熟”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from theatrical terminology, where "pat" means an actor has fully memorized their lines and can perform them flawlessly. In this context, using this phrase means that someone has mastered a skill or knowledge to the point where they can execute it effortlessly.

examples.en: She has the whole presentation down pat and can deliver it without any notes.
examples.cn: 她已经完全掌握了整个演讲，可以毫不依赖笔记地进行。

examples.en: I've got my morning routine down pat, it takes me only 15 minutes to get ready.
examples.cn: 我的晨间习惯已经驾轻就熟，只需15分钟就能准备好。

examples.en: He has the recipe down pat and makes the dish perfectly every time.
examples.cn: 他已经完全掌握了这道菜的食谱，每次都能做得很完美。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于戏剧术语，其中 “pat” 表示演员已经完全记住了台词，并且可以完美地表演出来。在这个背景下，使用这个短语意味着某人已经非常熟练地掌握了一项技能或知识，达到无需思考即可完成的程度。

title: Have the world by the tail

definition.cn: “拥有全世界” 或 “掌控一切”。
definition.en: This phrase originated in early 20th-century America and is used to describe a person who is in a very advantageous and controlling position. In such a scenario, the individual feels they can manage their life and surroundings, as if they have grabbed the world by the tail.

examples.en: After landing his dream job, he felt like he had the world by the tail.
examples.cn: 在得到梦寐以求的工作后，他感觉自己掌控了一切。

examples.en: With her talents and opportunities, she truly has the world by the tail.
examples.cn: 凭借她的才华和机会，她确实掌控了一切。

examples.en: Starting his own business made him feel like he had the world by the tail.
examples.cn: 创办自己的公司让他觉得自己掌控了一切。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于 20 世纪早期的美国，常用于描述一个人处于极其有利和具掌控的位置。在这种情况下，个人感觉自己能够掌握或控制自己的生活和周围的各种事物，如同抓住了世界的尾巴一样。

definition.en: This phrase is used to describe someone being free from their usual work or daily burdens, having free time to rest or do other things. It can refer to official leave, such as taking time off work, or can simply mean being temporarily free from any responsibilities.

examples.en: I need to have some time off to relax and recharge.
examples.cn: 我需要休假一下来放松并充电。

examples.en: Do you have any time off next week to meet up?
examples.cn: 你下周有空闲时间见面吗？

examples.en: She decided to have time off work to travel.
examples.cn: 她决定休假去旅行。

origin.cn: 这个短语用于描述某人脱离平时的工作或日常负担，有空闲时间来休息或做其他事情。它可以指正式的休假，比如请假，也可以指临时有空或者有一定时间不被任何责任束缚。

definition.en: This phrase literally means having two left feet, suggesting that a person is very clumsy or uncoordinated when it comes to dancing or physical activities. It is often used to describe those who are not good at dancing, frequently stepping on the wrong foot or tripping. It can also generally refer to someone who is exceptionally clumsy or lacks skill in certain activities.

examples.en: When it comes to dancing, John has two left feet.
examples.cn: 说到跳舞，约翰简直笨手笨脚。

examples.en: She tried to join the dance class, but she has two left feet.
examples.cn: 她试图加入舞蹈课，但她跳得很笨拙。

examples.en: Don't worry if you have two left feet, everyone gets better with practice.
examples.cn: 别担心你笨手笨脚的，每个人都能通过练习变得更好。

origin.cn: 这个短语字面意思是拥有两个左脚，意味着一个人在跳舞或运动时非常笨拙或不协调。它通常用来形容那些不擅长舞蹈、经常踩错步子或容易摔倒的人。这一表达也可以泛指在某些活动中显得特别笨拙或缺乏技能的人。

title: Have your head in the clouds

definition.en: This phrase's historical background is relatively unclear, but it is generally thought to describe someone who seems to be daydreaming, with their thoughts not on their current task or surroundings. It can also describe someone whose ideas are unrealistic and overly idealistic.

examples.en: He's always got his head in the clouds during meetings.
examples.cn: 他在会议中总是心不在焉。

examples.en: If you keep having your head in the clouds, you'll never finish your work on time.
examples.cn: 如果你继续心不在焉，你绝对赶不完工作。

examples.en: She tends to have her head in the clouds instead of focusing on practical matters.
examples.cn: 她倾向于不切实际，而不是关注实在的问题。

origin.cn: 这个短语的历史背景相对模糊，但一般认为它形容一个人好像在做白日梦，心思不在当前的工作或者周围的环境中。也可以用来描述一个人想法不切实际，过于理想化。

title: He has bigger fish to fry

definition.cn: “他有更重要的事情要做” 或 “他有更大的事要忙”。
definition.en: This idiom originated in the 17th century when people used "bigger fish to fry" to describe having more important tasks than the current one. The phrase comes from the culinary world, where if one has a bigger or more important fish to cook, smaller problems are usually set aside.

examples.en: He didn't attend the meeting because he has bigger fish to fry at the moment.
examples.cn: 他没有参加会议，因为他现在有更重要的事情要处理。

examples.en: Sure, you can ask him for help, but he might have bigger fish to fry.
examples.cn: 当然，你可以请他帮忙，但他可能有更重要的事情要做。

examples.en: Don't bother him with that issue; he has bigger fish to fry.
examples.cn: 别用那个问题打扰他了，他有更重要的事要忙。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于17世纪，当时人们用 “bigger fish to fry” 来形容有比当前事情更重要的任务。这个表达方式源自烹饪领域，当有更大或更重要的鱼要煮时，人们通常会把较小的问题放在一边。

title: He who laughs last laughs loudest

definition.cn: “笑到最后的人笑得最好” 或 “最后得胜者才是最终赢家”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from a folk proverb emphasizing the importance of perseverance. While some may appear to have the upper hand at the beginning, the true victors are those who can endure until the end. It teaches people to look at the long term and not be misled by temporary failures or successes.

examples.en: John didn't do well in the early rounds, but he who laughs last laughs loudest—he won the championship.
examples.cn: 约翰在前几轮表现不好，但笑到最后才是胜利者——他最终赢得了冠军。

examples.en: Don't be discouraged by the setbacks; remember, he who laughs last laughs loudest.
examples.cn: 不要被挫折打败，记住，笑到最后的人笑得最好。

examples.en: They underestimated her abilities, but she proved them wrong; he who laughs last laughs loudest.
examples.cn: 他们低估了她的能力，但她证明了他们是错的，笑到最后的人笑得最好。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自于民间谚语，强调持之以恒的重要性。尽管有人可能在一开始占上风或看似占优势，但真正赢得胜利的是那些能够坚持到最后的人。它教导人们要看长远，不要被暂时的失败或成功所迷惑。

title: He's a chip off the old block

definition.cn: “他是有其父必有其子” 或 “他特别像他父亲”。
definition.en: This idiom originates from the woodworking analogy. When you chip off a piece of wood from a larger block, the smaller chip retains the same grain and characteristics as the larger block. Accordingly, when someone (typically a son) is very similar to their father, this expression is used.

examples.en: He's a chip off the old block – just as stubborn as his father.
examples.cn: 他真是有其父必有其子——和他父亲一样固执。

examples.en: Like father, like son. He's truly a chip off the old block.
examples.cn: 正如父亲一样。他确实是个有其父必有其子。

examples.en: You can tell he's a chip off the old block by the way he handles business.
examples.cn: 你可以从他处理业务的方式看出他是有其父必有其子。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自木工的比喻。当你从一个大木块上削下一小块时，这小块儿带有和大木块相同的质地和纹理。因此，当一个人（通常是儿子）表现得和他的父亲非常相似时，人们会使用这个表达。

title: He's not playing with a full deck

definition.cn: “他不太正常” 或 “他精神有问题”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from card games. If someone is “not playing with a full deck,” it means they are missing some crucial cards that would make it impossible to play the game properly. This metaphorically extends to mean that a person is lacking something important in their behavior or thinking, making their actions or thoughts seem abnormal or illogical.

examples.en: After hearing his bizarre theory, I started to think he's not playing with a full deck.
examples.cn: 听了他那奇怪的理论后，我开始认为他精神有问题。

examples.en: When he tried to convince us that the earth is flat, it was clear he's not playing with a full deck.
examples.cn: 当他试图说服我们地球是平的时，很明显他不太正常。

examples.en: I swear he's not playing with a full deck if he thinks he can finish that project alone in one day.
examples.cn: 如果他觉得可以一天内独自完成那个项目，我敢说他精神有问题。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到纸牌游戏。如果有人 “没有用全副牌” 玩游戏，那么他明显缺少一些至关重要的牌，使得他无法正常进行游戏。这引申为一个人在行为或思维上缺少一些重要的元素，导致他的行动或思维显得异常或不合逻辑。

definition.en: This phrase traces back to the 19th century. Originally, "rocker" referred to a rocking chair, and "off his rocker" figuratively meant that someone had fallen off their rocking chair, implying they were mentally unstable or behaving unusually. With a touch of humor or playfulness, this phrase is often used in informal settings to describe someone acting in a strange or irrational manner.

examples.en: Don't listen to him, he's off his rocker.
examples.cn: 别听他的，他疯了。

examples.en: She's been acting like she's off her rocker lately.
examples.cn: 她最近的行为看起来像是疯了。

examples.en: After hearing his wild plan, I thought he was off his rocker.
examples.cn: 听到他那疯狂的计划后，我觉得他不正常。

origin.cn: 这个短语的起源可以追溯到 19 世纪。原本，“rocker” 是指摇椅，而 “off his rocker” 形象地表示一个人从摇椅上掉下来了，暗喻他精神失常或行为异常。加入幽默或俏皮的成分，这个短语常用于非正式场合，表达某人行为不合常理或显得怪异。

definition.en: The idiom originates from a physical height comparison: if someone is "head and shoulders above" another person, their head and shoulders are higher than the other's, indicating they are taller. This metaphor is used to describe someone's significant advantage and superiority in certain areas.

examples.en: In terms of problem-solving skills, Jane is head and shoulders above her peers.
examples.cn: 在解决问题的能力上，简遥遥领先于她的同龄人。

examples.en: The new model is head and shoulders above the old one in terms of performance.
examples.cn: 新型号的性能大大优于旧型号。

examples.en: His dedication to work is head and shoulders above anyone else's on the team.
examples.cn: 他对工作的敬业精神远远超过团队中的任何人。

origin.cn: 这个短语源于物理高度的比较：如果一个人 “head and shoulders above” 另一个人，那么他们的头和肩膀都高于对方，这表明他们比对方高出一截。这个比喻被用来形容人在某些方面的明显优势和超过别人之处。

definition.en: This phrase originates from the Spanish word “jefe,” which was transliterated into Japanese as “班長” or “酋長,” meaning leader or chief. Over time, this term was adopted into English and gradually evolved into "head honcho," used to refer to the highest leader or the most important person in an organization or group. The phrase is commonly used in informal settings, often carrying a light-hearted or humorous tone.

examples.en: The head honcho will be in town next week for the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 大佬下周会来城里参加年度会议。

examples.en: You'll need approval from the head honcho to proceed with the project.
examples.cn: 你需要得到头头的批准才能继续推进这个项目。

examples.en: Everyone looks up to the head honcho for guidance and decisions.
examples.cn: 每个人都仰望头头，寻求指引和决策。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自西班牙语单词 “jefe”，在日语中被转译为 “班长” 或 “酋长”，意思是领袖或首领。随着时间的推移，这个短语被引入英语并且逐渐演变成 “head honcho”，用来指代某个组织或团体中的最高领导人或最重要的人物。这个短语常用于非正式场合，具有一种轻松、玩笑的语气。

definition.en: This phrase indicates someone is not paying attention or is daydreaming, rather than focusing on practical matters. The imagery for this idiom comes from the idea of a person standing with their head in the clouds, appearing disconnected from reality.

examples.en: He always has his head in the clouds during meetings.
examples.cn: 他开会时总是心不在焉。

examples.en: She's a dreamer with her head in the clouds, but she has great ideas.
examples.cn: 她是个梦想家，虽然有点不切实际，但主意很棒。

examples.en: You can't have your head in the clouds if you want to succeed in business.
examples.cn: 如果你想在生意上成功，就不能心不在焉。

origin.cn: 这个短语表示某人心思不集中，或者沉浸在自己的幻想与梦想之中，而不是着眼于现实问题。这个短语的意象来源于，想象一个人站在那里，但头却在云层中，显得与现实脱节。

definition.en: Originally, this phrase was used to describe someone falling or tumbling in a topsy-turvy manner. However, nowadays it is often used to express a state of being completely infatuated or overtaken by love. It depicts that intense passion and enthusiasm where the object of affection becomes almost an all-consuming part of one's life.

examples.en: He's head over heels in love with her.
examples.cn: 他对她神魂颠倒。

examples.en: She fell head over heels for the charming artist.
examples.cn: 她为那个迷人的艺术家彻底迷恋。

examples.en: They are head over heels in their relationship, always together.
examples.cn: 他们在恋爱中神魂颠倒，总是形影不离。

origin.cn: 这个短语原本用于描述人们以倒头足倒置的方式跌倒或翻滚。然而，现在人们通常用它来表达一个人因爱或迷恋而完全失去自我控制的状态。它描绘的是那种极度的热情和激情，使得爱恋对象几乎成为生活的全部。

definition.en: This phrase originates from baseball and other sports, where it signals players to raise their heads and be alert for the ball. Today, this phrase is commonly used informally to refer to giving someone advance notice or a warning about something so they can be prepared.

examples.en: Thanks for the heads-up about the meeting tomorrow.
examples.cn: 谢谢你提醒我明天的会议。

examples.en: I just wanted to give you a heads-up that the boss is in a bad mood today.
examples.cn: 我只是想提醒你一下，老板今天心情不好。

examples.en: She gave me a heads-up about the traffic jam on my usual route.
examples.cn: 她提醒我在我平时的路线上有堵车。

origin.cn: 这个短语来源于棒球和其他体育活动，表示让队员提高警觉、准备好接受球。如今，这个短语被广泛用于非正式的交流中，用来指对某件事情的事先提醒或通知，以便接收者能够做好准备应对。

definition.cn: “通过小道消息听说” 或 “听到传闻”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the American Civil War period when the telegraph lines, which were used to transmit messages, were sometimes referred to as "grapevines" due to their winding nature. Over time, this expression evolved to mean receiving information through unofficial channels and hearsay.

examples.en: I heard it on the grapevine that they are planning to merge with another company.
examples.cn: 我通过小道消息听说他们计划与另一家公司合并。

examples.en: She heard it on the grapevine that her favorite teacher is leaving school.
examples.cn: 她听到传闻说她最喜欢的老师要离开学校了。

examples.en: You can't trust everything you hear on the grapevine.
examples.cn: 你不能相信所有的小道消息。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于美国南北战争时期，当时传输信息的电报线路因其弯弯曲曲的样子被戏称为 “葡萄藤（grapevine）”。随着时间的推移，这个表达逐渐演变成我们如今所知的小道消息和非正式渠道传递信息的意思。

title: Hear something straight from the horse's mouth

definition.cn: “直接从权威或第一手来源获得信息”。
definition.en: This phrase originates from the horse racing industry, where buyers would check the horse's teeth or ask the trainer to get accurate information about the horse's age and health, which is the most direct and reliable source. In modern usage, it means getting information directly from someone who has authoritative or first-hand knowledge, rather than through indirect or second-hand sources.

examples.en: I heard the news straight from the horse’s mouth; the CEO himself confirmed it.
examples.cn: 我直接从权威消息来源得知这个消息，CEO 本人亲自证实了。

examples.en: You can trust the information because it’s straight from the horse’s mouth.
examples.cn: 你可以相信这个信息，因为它是直接从权威来源得到的。

examples.en: I prefer to get my updates straight from the horse’s mouth rather than rely on rumors.
examples.cn: 我更愿意直接从可靠来源获得更新，而不是依赖谣言。

origin.cn: 这个短语源自赛马行业，买家在购买一匹马时，往往会从马的饲养员或直接观察马的牙齿来了解马的年龄及健康状况，也就是从最直接、最可靠的源头获取信息。在现代用法中，这个短语表示直接从可信赖的或有专业知识的来源获取信息，而不是通过辗转传达。

definition.en: This phrase originated in the 1920s America when cartoonist Billy DeBeck and The New York Times jointly published comics and texts where this phrase was first used, and it gradually became widely popular. The term "heebie-jeebies" is typically used to describe a strong psychological and physiological reaction due to fear, nervousness, or unease.

examples.en: The creepy old house gave me the heebie-jeebies.
examples.cn: 那座阴森的旧房子让我感到毛骨悚然。

examples.en: Spiders always give me the heebie-jeebies.
examples.cn: 蜘蛛总是让我感到很不安。

examples.en: Watching that horror movie last night gave me the heebie-jeebies.
examples.cn: 昨晚看那部恐怖片让我感到非常紧张。

origin.cn: 这个短语起源于1920年代美国，当时漫画家比利·德法与《纽约时报》联合发表的漫画和文本里首次使用了这个短语，后来逐渐广泛流传。短语 “heebie-jeebies” 通常用来形容由于恐惧、紧张或者不安而产生的强烈心理和生理反应。

definition.en: This phrase is used to describe something scattered in different places or locations. Its origin is quite straightforward, as "here" means "this place" and "there" means "that place." Combined, they form the idea of something being present in multiple locations. This expression is commonly used to describe elements, features, or activities that are not centralized but spread out.

examples.en: We found small cafes here and there in the city.
examples.cn: 我们在城市的各处发现了小咖啡馆。

examples.en: He has friends here and there around the world.
examples.cn: 他在世界各地都有朋友。

examples.en: You can find wildflowers here and there in the meadow.
examples.cn: 你可以在草地上到处找到野花。

origin.cn: 这个短语用于形容某物或某人分布在不同地点或地方。其起源具有日常性，因为 “*here*” 表示 “这里”，而 “*there*” 表示 “那里”，合在一起就是 “到处” 的意思。这种表达方式用于描述某些元素，特质，或活动不集中于一个地点，而是散布在各地。
